summary: Duplicate of the just-published article covering vlt 1.0's launch (same event, same day, same core facts, same HN quotes) — no meaningfully new information or angle; human editor overrides the automated APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS verdict per the originality rule.

findings.details: This submission covers the exact same news event as src/content/articles/2026-09/07-vlt-reaches-10-launching-hosted-package-registries-as-a-security-first-npm-replacement.md, published to main just prior to this review (PR #2361, merged 2026-09-07). Both articles report vlt's 1.0 launch using the same core facts (phased vlt install/vlt build split, 60+ query selectors with ~half security-focused, 275k flagged malicious package versions with 25%+ still available on npm, '38% faster' registry performance, BSD-2-Clause-Patent license) and even the same Hacker News exchange with founder Darcy Clarke ('5s: save time & money'). Three of this submission's four sources (InfoQ, vlt.io/blog/1-0, the HN thread) are identical URLs to sources already cited in the published article. This is a REJECT-level duplicate per Step 5 of review-submission.md, not a case where APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS could honestly cover the issue — there is no single correctable defect, the entire submission is redundant coverage.

content_preview.title: vlt 1.0 Ships as an npm-Compatible Package Registry With Phased Installs and Malware-Blocking
content_preview.summary: vlt, built by npm's original developers, launched a 1.0 client and hosted registry that splits install from script execution and blocks flagged malware before delivery.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

vlt, a JavaScript package manager and registry built by the original creators of npm, has released vlt 1.0, shipping as a drop-in npm replacement alongside the general availability of its hosted package registries and ecosystem mirrors, according to [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/vlt-npm-replacement/). The company's own announcement, published by founder and CEO Darcy Clarke on the [vlt blog](https://www.vlt.io/blog/1-0), says the release makes vlt "now an end-to-end pla...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News-category piece (720 words, within the 400-1200 range), clear Overview/What We Know/Context/What We Don't Know sections, professional tone, no AI self-reference detected.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200, no suspicious_patterns) and read in full from their gzipped snapshots in sources/2026-09/vlt-10-ships-as-an-npm-compatible-package-registry-with-phased-installs-and-malware-blocking/: source-0.html.gz (InfoQ) confirms the phased install/build split, the 275,000+ flagged package versions with a quarter still installable on npm, and the 38% faster registry claim verbatim ('flagged more than 275,000 package versions, a quarter of which reviewers note are still installable on npm... vlt reports its registry as up to 38% faster than npm'). source-1.html.gz (vlt.io/blog/1-0) confirms the phased-installations mechanism verbatim ('Phased installations allow vlt install to download without running scripts; and vlt build to run selectively, blocking known malware by default'), the '275k' and '25%' figures verbatim, and the list of query selectors (:malware, :cve, :unmaintained, :outdated, :eval, :fs, :license, :vuln, :peer, :dist()) verbatim. source-2.html.gz (vlt.io homepage) confirms the 38% figure and the 12.0s vs 19.4s Astro-project benchmark numbers verbatim. source-3.html.gz (Hacker News thread) confirms both quoted comments verbatim ('This will benefit the entire ecosystem', 'I am not sure exactly what this service is or why it is desirable. Pitch me in five seconds or less?') and the founder's reply verbatim ('5s: save time & money'). No hallucinated quotes, no misattribution found — every direct quote and specific in the submission traces to its cited source.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All claims verified against source snapshots as described above. No fabrications or unsupported specifics found. The submission is factually sound on its own merits.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; no sensationalism or editorializing.
editor_notes.originality: REJECTED ON THIS BASIS. Direct comparison against src/content/articles/2026-09/07-vlt-reaches-10-launching-hosted-package-registries-as-a-security-first-npm-replacement.md (published on main via PR #2361, merged immediately before this review): both pieces cover vlt's 1.0 launch as the central event, both lead with the same 'built by npm's original developers' framing, both report the identical phased vlt-install/vlt-build split, the identical 60+/~half-security-focused query-selector detail (with overlapping named selectors :malware, :cve, :unmaintained, :outdated, :eval, :fs, :license, :vuln, :peer, :dist()), the identical 275k-flagged/25%-still-available malware figures, the identical '38% faster' registry performance claim, the identical BSD-2-Clause-Patent license fact, and the identical Hacker News thread — quoting the same founder reply ('5s: save time & money' / 'save time & money'). Three of this submission's four source URLs (InfoQ, vlt.io/blog/1-0, the HN thread) are byte-identical URLs to sources already cited in the published article. The only incremental details in this submission not present in the published article are the specific 12.0s-vs-19.4s Astro benchmark numbers, the --view=mermaid rendering flag, and a passing mention of a Socket integration for the security selectors — none of which amount to a distinct angle, a new development, or significant new information; they are minor supporting details on the same story. This fails the Step 5 originality bar: 'the same news with no new information or angle.'
concerns: This submission covers the exact same launch event as the article published moments earlier from PR #2361, with heavily overlapping sources, quotes, and figures. No meaningfully new angle or information distinguishes it from the already-published coverage.
3 of 4 sources (vlt.io/blog/1-0, vlt.io homepage, Hacker News thread) are not on config/source_allowlist.txt, though this is secondary to the originality rejection.
recommendations: Reject and close without merge; do not create an article-meta or corrections file since the article will not publish.

If the contributor bot wants to cover vlt 1.0 from a genuinely distinct angle (e.g., third-party adoption reaction, a technical deep-dive on the Socket-powered selectors, or a follow-up once adoption data exists), it should submit that as new, clearly differentiated coverage rather than resubmitting this story.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Factually sound and well-sourced submission that would otherwise merit APPROVE, but it is a same-day duplicate of already-published coverage of the identical event (vlt 1.0 launch) with substantially overlapping sources and facts. REJECT per the originality rule in review-submission.md Step 5 — this is not a single-correction defect, so APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS is not appropriate; the entire submission is redundant with existing coverage.
